answer: Rental Decay Schedule.** Each identity must anchor a hardware-rooted security module whose attestation key signs every action. The cipher rotates per epoch, forcing re-attestation under fresh keys. Attacker cost scales with two multiplied terms: module rental per identity and re-attestation frequency. A velvet floor raises rental cost sharply after the first hundred identities, so bare identities cost more than productive ones. Enforcement: actions from identities missing a current cipher are dropped, not flagged.
